utility.value: Xcel Energy (Public Service Company of Colorado) for addresses Xcel serves. Summit County's PV checklist also names Mountain Parks Electric. Check the utility named on your electric bill.
utility.notes: Xcel Energy's list of Colorado communities served (10/2015) shows Frisco with gas and electricity service. The list is by community name, not by address. The Town lists Xcel Energy, 970-262-4050, among the agencies whose approval may be needed for permits. Neither source says that Xcel serves every address in Frisco, and Summit County's photovoltaic submittal checklist has a line that names Mountain Parks Electric ("Mountain Parks Electric Under 25 kW required"). Confirm the utility named on your electric bill before you apply for interconnection.

value.name: Xcel Energy
value.notes: Applies only to addresses served by Xcel Energy. Check the utility named on your electric bill. Xcel says all solar customers receive net energy metering benefits, and any excess is held in a virtual bank to be applied against future bills.

county.notes: The Town's pages name Summit County as the office that handles solar and electrical permits, but they do not state in a sentence which county the Town is in.

permit_authority.value: Summit County Building Inspection Department (solar permits for the Town of Frisco)
permit_authority.notes: The Town says solar applications for the Town of Frisco are handled by the Summit County Building Department. Summit County receives the application, takes in the fee, refers the permit to Summit Fire and the Town for approval, issues the permit and performs the inspections. Electrical permitting and inspections for the Town are also provided by the Summit County Building Department. Other Town building permits are handled by Comprehensive Building Code Services, LLC, which took on the former Town Building Division's responsibilities in August 2024.

permit_url.notes: This is Summit County's Building Permits page, where the Town points solar applicants for the application forms. Under Technical Permits it says photovoltaic permits are required for solar systems. Building and technical permits should be submitted in person by a representative who can answer submittal questions.

interconnection_url.notes: For Xcel Energy customers. Xcel says that once you understand state, local and utility requirements and permits, you can submit an interconnection application online. In most cases the developer or installer submits the application on your behalf, or you can manage your own. The customer's name on the application must match the name on the Xcel Energy account or bill. Xcel highly recommends that construction of your system should not start until the application receives full approval from its engineering team and all final agreements are signed. Xcel says the work ends with a permission to operate letter to the generator owner, which is separate from the Summit County permit and inspections.

value.name: Renewable Battery Connect
value.description: Xcel says that when you add an eligible solar charged battery and participate, you let Xcel automatically manage your battery during periods of peak demand on the grid. Upfront incentive, General: $250 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to $5,000 per application). Income Qualified: $1,000 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). Disproportionately Impacted Community: $500 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). There is also a $100 annual participation incentive for participating in control events (for 5 years).
value.eligibility: For Xcel Energy customers adding an eligible solar charged battery to a home or small business. Xcel says eligible equipment includes all Tesla Powerwall models or all current Enphase models.

battery_programs.notes: Xcel's page shows budget available for 2026 on figures dated 11/02/2026.

value.name: Summit County Photovoltaic Permit Application (DC side)
Technical Permit Application marked "Photovoltaic-AC" (AC electrical permit)
value.required_when: For the separate electrical permit for the AC side of the system.

value.name: Site plan to scale showing the major components
Property lines and setbacks (ground-mounted systems)
Engineer-stamped structural evaluation of the roof (roof-mounted systems)
value.required_when: Roof-mounted systems. The County's 2020 sheet describes it as an engineer-stamped letter confirming roof and wind load can hold the PV system.

value.name: Engineer-stamped one-line or three-line electrical drawing
value.required_when: All systems. It must show the PV array configuration, wiring, grounding, overcurrent protection, inverter, rapid shut-down, disconnects, batteries, required signs and the AC point of connection.

value.name: Engineer stamp verifying wind speed and snow load for the Town of Frisco
value.required_when: The checklist asks for a minimum of 90 mph/1000 pascals wind speed and 80 psf/3831 pascals snow load for the Town of Frisco.

value.name: Roof plan with the location of all PV panels and roof access pathways (roof-mounted systems)
Manufacturer's specification sheets for all components
value.required_when: All systems. The checklist says this includes PV modules (UL 1703, snow loads up to 5400 Pa and wind load up to 2400 Pa), inverters (UL1741), rapid shutdown, combiner box, disconnects, batteries and mounting systems (UL2703), and the design operating temperature must be suitable for -13 degrees.

value.name: Elevations (ground-mounted or pole-mounted systems)
Completed fire district sign-off card
value.required_when: Returned to the Summit County Building Department before the photovoltaic permit can be issued.

value.name: Summit Fire & EMS fire department permit
value.required_when: Summit Fire & EMS's permit letter, which the Town links as its 2020 help letter, says a fire department permit is required for all solar. Summit Fire & EMS's current Permits page does not list solar among the projects that need its permits, and the Town says the County refers solar permits to Summit Fire. Ask Summit County whether a separate Summit Fire & EMS permit is needed.

required_documents.notes: Items are from Summit County's Photovoltaic Permit Submittal Completeness Checklist (2023), its Photovoltaic Systems Permitting Information sheet (revised 4/13/2020) and Summit Fire & EMS's permit letter. The checklist says all applicable items are required in order to submit.

value: Bring the photovoltaic permit application and all submittal documents in person to the Summit County Building Inspection Department at 0037 Peak One Dr., Frisco. The County says a representative who can answer submittal questions should submit them, and it does not accept emailed or mailed documents.
Pay the fees when you submit. The County says fees are due at the time of submittal and payment for plan review is required at the time of submittal.
The permit technician checks the submittal, and the contractor takes a sign-off card to the fire district for review and returns the completed card to the County.
Summit County refers the permit to Summit Fire and the Town of Frisco for approval.
Summit County reviews the plans and issues the photovoltaic (DC) permit.
After the photovoltaic permit is issued, the County issues the AC electrical permit over the counter.

If Xcel Energy serves your address, your contractor (or you) submits the interconnection application to Xcel Energy. Xcel highly recommends not starting construction until the application is fully approved and all final agreements are signed.
Schedule inspections online in eTRAKiT, including a rough electrical inspection if any electrical work will later be concealed.
When ready for final, schedule the final electrical inspections for the DC and AC permits on the same date.
If Xcel Energy serves your address, Xcel works with you and your contractors to witness test and energize the system, and the work ends with a permission to operate letter to the generator owner.
inspection_steps.notes: The Summit County permits, the County's final electrical inspections and your electric utility's permission to operate (for Xcel Energy customers, Xcel's permission to operate letter) are separate approvals. The County's 2020 sheet says every photovoltaic permit needs a plan review, while its current Building Permits page says residential roof-mounted systems under 15kw may be issued over the counter. Ask the County which path applies to your system.

value.notes: Summit County's Photovoltaic Systems Permitting Information sheet (revised 4/13/2020) says the Building Department reviews the documents within 10 business days from the day following submittal. The 10 business days start once all required documents are submitted and the plan review fee is paid. The County's current Building Permits page says residential roof-mounted systems under 15kw may be issued over the counter if all submittal materials are provided, which differs from the 2020 sheet.

value.program_or_pathway: Summit County photovoltaic (DC) permit plus AC electrical permit
other_conditions: Summit County's current Building Permits page says residential roof-mounted systems under 15kw may be issued over the counter if all submittal materials are provided, while its 2020 sheet says a plan review is required. Confirm with the County.
A plan review is required for all residential PV systems over 15kw, ground-mounted and commercial systems.
The contractor installing the DC system must be registered with Summit County as an alternative energy contractor, which requires proof of NABCEP certification as a PV installer.
The electrical contractor pulling the AC permit must be registered with Summit County as an electrical contractor.
The Town does not require a contractor's license, but all contractors working in Frisco must have a current Town of Frisco Business License.

For electrical permits, Summit County requires a Town of Frisco building permit number before it accepts the application. Ask Summit County whether this applies to the AC electrical permit for a solar system.
Photovoltaic and electrical permit applications expire 180 days after the date of application, and permits expire 18 months after issuance.
Roof pathways: not less than two 36-inch pathways from the low roof edge to the ridge, one 36-inch pathway on the street or driveway side, and a 36-inch ridge setback unless an exception is met.
Carbon monoxide alarms are required in single-family and multifamily dwelling units when any project requiring a permit is done on the property.
The Town's solar page says the Colorado Solar/Wind Easements and Rights Law, passed in 1979, prevents any residential covenants that restrict solar access.
Xcel Energy sizing rule for net metering (not a permit rule): expected generation, combined with other generation at the address, may not exceed 200% of the previous 12 months of consumption.

value.name: Summit County photovoltaic permit, residential plan review
Summit County photovoltaic permit, residential permit fee
Maximum total solar permit fee, residential
value.notes: The Town says Summit County takes in the fee, a maximum total permit fee of $500. The County's 2020 sheet says the DC and AC permit fees combined shall not exceed $500 for residential projects.

permit_fees.notes: The two County amounts are from the Photovoltaic Permit Fees table on Summit County's Building Permit Fee Schedule page, which prints no effective date next to them. The County's 2020 sheet says the DC permit fee is based on the total valuation of the system plus the cost of the solar panels, and that a plan review is required for every photovoltaic permit. The County's current Building Permits page says residential roof-mounted systems under 15kw may be issued over the counter if all submittal materials are provided. Neither page says whether the $175.00 plan review fee applies to a system issued over the counter, so ask the County. The Town of Frisco 2026 fee schedule (Town Council adoption date December 9, 2025) also lists a Residential Photovoltaic Permit at "$303.05/$196.95 State allowable fees". The Town's solar pages say Summit County takes in the permit fee, so ask Summit County which amounts apply to your permit. The County's 2020 sheet says the AC electrical permit fee is based on the valuation of the AC side, with no plan review fee. Summit County says fees are due at the time of submittal, and a processing fee of $.75 plus 2.25% applies to credit card payments. The Town says that for solar the applicant no longer brings materials to the Town, Summit Fire and Summit County for separate permits and pays separate fees. Summit Fire & EMS's permit letter lists a permit fee and says a fire department permit is required for all solar, so ask Summit County whether any separate fee applies.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Income Qualified upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says customers who qualify under the terms of Income Qualified can receive an upfront rebate of $3 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer and qualify under Xcel's Income Qualified terms.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Disproportionately Impacted Communities upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says Disproportionately Impacted Communities can receive an upfront rebate of $0.50 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer.

value.name: Solarize Summit rebate
value.description: The Town says Frisco residents and businesses are eligible to participate in the Solarize Summit program to receive up to $1,500 in rebates for installing solar. The page says the 2023 program is sold out for Breckenridge and Summit County homeowners, but HC3 still has a few $1500 rebates for Frisco residents. The page refers to the 2023 program, describes Solarize Summit as a limited-time discount and gives no end date, so ask HC3 whether rebates remain.
value.eligibility: Town of Frisco residents and businesses installing solar through the Solarize Summit program.

rebates.notes: The Solar*Rewards rebates are Xcel Energy programs. Xcel's page says that as of 10/05/2026 it moved $1,050,000 from Solar*Rewards C&I to the Solar*Rewards Residential IQ/DIC program.
